aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-he.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health
aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-he.note: Culturally safe care run by and for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, plus primary care and hospital services with Aboriginal Health Workers and Aboriginal Liaison Officers. If you are Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander and have a Medicare card, you can get a free 715 health check every year at an Aboriginal Medical Service or bulk-billing clinic. Ask your GP or Aboriginal Health Practitioner about Closing the Gap PBS co-payment support too (check eligibility): after a one-off registration, people who usually pay full price for PBS medicines pay the concession price, and people who usually pay the concession price pay nothing. Our health check tool shows other free checks and vaccines.

interests: GP clinic: general practice and primary health care
715 health check (needed before using Awabakal dental)
Chronic disease management
Antenatal clinic; men's, women's and children's health
Immunisations and preventive health screening
Allied health and visiting specialists
Mental health and social wellbeing support; Wiyala social and emotional wellbeing (SEWB), family wellbeing, psychology and psychiatry
Dental at Hamilton (most dental services free)
Transport for aged care patients to medical, dental and specialist appointments (book 24 hours ahead)
Quit smoking support (Tackling Indigenous Smoking)
Monday to Friday 8:30am to 5pm; wheelchair accessible
inclusive: Aims to provide care to “Aboriginal people and their families in our community”
“Awabakal Medical Service bulk bills as long as you have a valid Medicare card.”

people.name: Ungooroo GP and Health Services
people.eligibility: GP services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and for non-Aboriginal people.
interests: GP clinic (general practice)
Disability, social and recreational activity service
Telehealth capable
AH&MRC member service (Aboriginal community controlled)

people.name: Hunter Primary Care: Aboriginal Care Coordination (CCSS)
people.eligibility: Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Newcastle and the Hunter with a complex long-term illness. Referral from a health professional only: ask your GP.
interests: Chronic disease care coordination (diabetes and related eye conditions, heart, lung and kidney disease, cancer, mental health)
A care coordinator helps you manage your health and wellbeing
Funding may be available for some health costs (assessed by your care coordinator)
Online lifestyle support groups with Aboriginal health workers, an exercise physiologist, dietitian, OTs and nurses
inclusive: For people who identify as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander; Aboriginal health workers support cultural wellbeing and safety in its lifestyle groups

people.name: Hunter Primary Care: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Worker Service
people.specialty: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Workers
people.eligibility: People who identify as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander. Self-referral online, or referral from your GP or health provider.
interests: Information about local health services
Help to reach community and social services
Referrals to culturally appropriate providers
Help getting to appointments with GPs, specialists, tests and allied health
inclusive: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Worker team, funded by the Hunter New England and Central Coast PHN

people.name: Yudhilidin (Hunter Primary Care)
people.specialty: Social and emotional wellbeing care coordination
people.eligibility: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people aged 16 and over whose mental health or wellbeing affects daily life, living in Newcastle, Port Stephens, Lake Macquarie or the lower Hunter. Self-referral or professional referral.
interests: Yudhilidin means guidance: culturally safe social and emotional wellbeing (SEWB) support
Time-limited care coordination by Aboriginal Peer Navigators, with clinical support as needed
Links to GPs, counsellors and psychologists, alcohol and other drug services, financial counselling, domestic and family violence support, housing and cultural connection groups
inclusive: “Culturally safe social and emotional wellbeing support” for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people

people.name: Integrated Team Care (ITC) Program
people.practice: Hunter New England and Central Coast PHN
people.eligibility: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people with chronic conditions such as heart disease, diabetes or COPD. The PHN page does not name local providers: ask your GP or Aboriginal Medical Service, or call the PHN.
interests: Integrated Team Care (ITC): “improves access to culturally appropriate, mainstream primary care services, including but not limited to, general practice, allied health and specialists”
Care coordinators (nurses or Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health workers) arrange GP care plan services and reviews, and faster access to allied health and specialists
Outreach workers encourage appointments and medication pick-up and arrange transport
Can help with GP-approved medical aids
inclusive: For Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people with chronic conditions (Australian Government ITC program)

people.name: Calvary Mater Newcastle: Aboriginal Hospital Liaison Officer
people.eligibility: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients and families at the hospital.
interests: Aboriginal Hospital Liaison Officer (brochure on the hospital site)
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander brochures for the oncology ward and the Psycho-Oncology Service
inclusive: Aboriginal Hospital Liaison Officer listed for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples

people.name: Hunter New England Health hospitals: Aboriginal Liaison Officers and Yallarwah Place
people.address: John Hunter Hospital, New Lambton Heights NSW 2305
people.eligibility: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients and families in NSW public hospitals, including John Hunter and Maitland. Yallarwah Place is for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients and families travelling to John Hunter Hospital.
interests: Aboriginal Liaison Officers: “If you’d like support from an Aboriginal Liaison Officer, just let a staff member know.”
Help talking with clinical staff, understanding your care and planning discharge
Yallarwah Place: culturally welcoming accommodation and support on the John Hunter Hospital grounds
inclusive: NSW Health: “Our hospitals are committed to providing culturally safe care for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.”
